pictures.author: Raimond Spekking
pictures.observed: Courtyard entrance: two long stone wings with tall window bays and pilasters, deep projecting cornice, large blank main wall, stepped roof and three rectangular rooftop elements, broad low glazed vestibule. Historical mapped entrance configuration; no copied lettering/signs.

pictures.author: Peter Christian Riemann
pictures.observed: View from opposite canal: surviving three-wing geometry, north end pilasters and tall round-headed lower windows with smaller upper windows, heavy cornices and stepped main roof. Entrance rebuilding/excavation and scaffolding are temporary context; future fourth wing not built into this model.

currentRoundInspection.scope: Pergamon Museum: complete connected mapped three-wing museum with open west court, limestone gallery wings with tall recessed glazing and pilasters, heavy cornices, hipped/stepped roof forms, central stepped entrance wall and roof lanterns, lower east service alcove and the mapped glazed entrance vestibule. This asset represents the mapped pre-renovation entrance configuration. The2026 picture informs surviving stone facades; construction pits, scaffolding, temporary signs and a future fourth wing are not reconstructed. Keep James-Simon-Galerie, Neues Museum, Bode Museum, surrounding colonnades, canal/quays and all unrelated buildings as context.
